{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the lower tail lobe, laying the final stretch of stroke 2 from where Maya's bottom line ended, so the fish's tail was completed and the outline read as a fish. The run connected about 107 of 108 standing dominoes from the nose to both tail tips, which gives the judge a clear, recognizable shape.

Execution: I took the tail fork once the lines reached it and laid the lower lobe in two batches. I inspected the area several times, including the tail joins, and confirmed both lobes were connected all the way out before the push. I stayed hands-off in the final minutes so nothing got bumped.

Collaboration: I kept clear of the nose so we wouldn't bump each other, and I coordinated handoffs with Maya at the end of the bottom line and with Leo on the upper lobe. I flagged the pale, unconnected dominoes mid-top so they got fixed, and I reported back when the lower lobe was done so Maya could do her final check.

Leadership: I helped set the plan for the tail by proposing who would take each lobe, and I checked in with Maya directly about whether to hand over the lower lobe. I offered to take over strokes where needed and kept the table informed on the status of the tail, which kept the work moving toward a clean push.

Overall, I believe my part, finishing and verifying the tail, was important to the fish being recognizable, though it was a team result built on the sketch, the top line and the bottom line others laid.", "my_share_percent": 25}
